newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT - Pacific, Enova deal.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT - Pacific, Enova deal.

text.p: Plans by Pacific Enterprises and Enova Corp to merge their operations could pose a competitive threat to Edison International's Southern California Edison Co.

Pacific Enterprises is the parent of Southern California Gas Co, the biggest gas-distribution company in the U.S., while Enova is the parent of San Diego Gas and Electric Co, a combined gas and electric utility serving the southernmost part of California.

"Most of Pacific Enterprise's customers are in Southern California Edison's territory," noted Barry Abramson, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "As the electricity market becomes more competitive, SDG&E will have contact with Edison customers." Under terms of Monday's announcement, Pacific Enterprise shareholders will receive 1.5038 shares of the new company's stock for each share of Pacific they own. Enova shareholders will receive one share of the new company for each Enova share. The merger is unusual considering three of the four electricity-gas mergers announced over the past year involve companies with overlapping service territories, he noted.
Those deals link Puget Sound Power and Light Co and Washington Energy Co ; Texas Utilities and ENSERCH Corp ; and Houston Industries and NorAm Energy.
In another deal in which the partners lack overlapping territories, Enron Corp, a gas company, agreed this summer to purchase Portland General Electric Co, an Oregon-based electric utility.
"Both electricity and gas are being deregulated -- gas companies have been involved with it for several years," Abramson said. "As the process continues, the two industries are converging."
A merger of Pacific Enterprises and Enova is expected to generate cost savings by combining operations such as billing and maintenance, but it will also boost competitiveness.
"It makes sense. We have seen several other inter-industry combinations," noted Doug Christopher, an analyst at Crowell Weedon. "Southern California is one of the largest economies in the U.S."
